name: Speak comfortably to a small group
blurb: Presenting to eight people around a table is a different skill from a stage: it is a conversation you happen to be leading, and it responds to structure and reps.
gear: Real opportunities: meetings, book clubs, team updates
steps: Prepare a structure, not a script: three points, an opening line and a closing line.
Fix your physical baseline: feet planted, hands visible and still when not gesturing, shoulders down.
Slow down deliberately and use silence instead of filler words. Pauses feel enormous to you and normal to everyone else.
Make eye contact with one person per sentence, moving around the group.
Invite interaction early — a question in the first minute changes the dynamic from performance to conversation.
Take every low-stakes opportunity to speak. Volume of reps is the only real cure for nerves.
tips: Nervousness is mostly invisible. What you feel as shaking, they see as normal.
Filler words disappear when you accept silence. Record yourself and count them.
proof: You lead a 10-minute discussion with a group, without notes, and can take questions comfortably.
